clue.text: Framed by narrow window, behold gallant knight

indicators.note: a picture framed by something sits inside it, so the short word goes within the window word

blocks.note: a lancet is a tall narrow pointed window
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: A chivalrous knight is glimpsed through a slit of a castle window.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue order misleads: it is the word for behold that is framed, sitting inside the window word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Lancelot is the most famous of King Arthur's Round Table knights, renowned for gallantry.

clue.text: One far from admirable character or another I upset

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is weighing up whether one unpleasant person or another has upset the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: An antihero is a central character who lacks conventional heroic virtues, so is far from admirable.

clue.text: A great deal of Tory party followed by half-hearted mob

indicators.note: a word with half its heart gone loses one of the two identical letters at its centre

blocks.note: Con is short for Conservative, the Tory party
a side is a party in a dispute or contest
a rabble is a disorderly crowd

explanation.surface: A political party's supporters are trailed by a lukewarm crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing one of the middle pair of Bs from the mob word leaves RABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Considerable' sums mean large ones, so the adjective substitutes for 'a great deal of'.

clue.text: Problem with hose that firemen often raise

blocks.note: first meaning: a run in stockings or tights
second meaning: the climbing frame fire crews put up against buildings

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hose' and 'firemen' together suggest a fire hose, but the hose here is hosiery.
explanation.definitionFit: A run in tights is called a ladder in Britain, and firefighters raise extending ladders to reach upper floors.

clue.text: Add colour with explosive stuff about one of the Romans

indicators.note: about means surrounding here, so the explosive goes around the Roman

blocks.note: TNT is trinitrotoluene, a high explosive
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone livens up a picture of Rome with fireworks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One of the Romans' is not a person but the Roman numeral for one.
explanation.definitionFit: To tint something is to give it a shade or hue, i.e. add colour.

clue.text: Frank view about paintings put up

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means written upwards, so the word runs backwards
about means surrounding here, so the view word encloses the other

blocks.note: a sight is a view
paintings collectively are art

explanation.surface: An honest opinion about pictures being hung on the wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Being straight with someone means being honest and direct, a synonym of frank.

clue.text: Fruit that bird can't get in tree

blocks.note: first meaning: a green fuzzy-skinned fruit
second meaning: a flightless New Zealand bird, which cannot fly up into branches

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a fruit out of reach; the second half describes the flightless bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The kiwi fruit and the flightless kiwi bird share a name; the bird cannot fly, so it cannot get up a tree.

clue.text: Small piece or scrap of cloth people wrapped in paper, initially

indicators.note: something wrapped in a covering sits inside it, so the cloth and people go inside the paper

blocks.note: a rag is a scrap of cloth
men are people
the Financial Times, known by its initials

explanation.surface: Someone describes a bit of fabric or bundled people in newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' does not take first letters; it means the paper is named by its initials, FT for the Financial Times.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragment is a small broken-off part of something, a small piece.

clue.text: Bury gold around island — not the coastal part

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the burial and gold words close about the island

blocks.note: to inter is to bury
I is the abbreviation for island
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Instructions for hiding treasure on an island, but away from the shore.
explanation.definitionFit: The interior of a country is its inland region, the part away from the coast.

clue.text: Crazy characters turned round in shock

indicators.note: something turned round faces the other way, so the word is read from the end

blocks.note: nuts are crazy people

explanation.surface: Lunatics wheel about in alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun someone is to daze or astonish them, a verb sense of shock.

clue.text: Creating distraction, wrongly directs a monarch

indicators.note: doing something wrongly means out of proper order, so these letters are muddled

blocks.note: taken as written
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: A courtier causes a diversion by misleading the king.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidetracking means diverting someone from the main issue, i.e. creating a distraction.

clue.text: Habitual thief and policeman endlessly take off together

indicators.note: endlessly means without an end, so the last letter of take is dropped
off means gone wrong or awry, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A compulsive thief and a constable escape together.
explanation.definitionFit: A kleptomaniac has a compulsive urge to steal, making them a habitual thief.

clue.text: Nurse visibly embarrassed about drug offered

indicators.note: about means surrounding here, so the joined words close around the drug

blocks.note: to tend is to nurse
E is ecstasy
embarrassment shows as a red face

explanation.surface: A nurse blushes over some medication.
explanation.walkthrough: The drug goes between the two words rather than inside a single one: nurse and embarrassed together form the outer shell.
explanation.definitionFit: To tender something is to formally offer it, as with a resignation or payment.

clue.text: Drunkard finally finished port

indicators.note: finally points to the very last letter of the word before it

blocks.note: last letter of drunkard
over means finished

explanation.surface: A drinker has polished off the last of the port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the drink to go with drunkard, but it is a harbour town. Dover is a Channel port in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Dover is England's main ferry port facing France.

clue.text: Place for putting European or English novelist

blocks.note: on a golf course you putt on the green
E abbreviates either European or English

explanation.surface: Someone wonders about the nationality of a writer who putts.
explanation.definitionFit: Graham Greene was an English novelist, author of Brighton Rock.

clue.text: Wild animal finding nothing in watering hole

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the zero sits within the drinking place

blocks.note: O looks like zero, nothing
a bar is a pub, a watering hole

explanation.surface: A beast arrives at a waterhole and finds it dry.
explanation.definitionFit: A boar is a wild pig, the classic wild animal of the forest hunt.

clue.text: Support getting over each awfully painful experience that's behind one

indicators.note: awfully means badly, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: to back is to support
taken as written

explanation.surface: Getting past a painful ordeal with help, so it's in the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind one' reads like 'in the past', but the pain is literally in your back. In a down clue, 'getting over' puts the support word on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Backache is pain in the back, which is literally behind you.

clue.text: Turned to leading man or lady, one playing central role

indicators.note: turned means facing the other way, so the words are read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
a VIP is a very important person, man or woman

explanation.surface: Someone looks to the star of a show, the one at its centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A pivot is the central point on which things turn, so figuratively someone with a central role.

clue.text: Salesman's pitches about new models

indicators.note: about means surrounding here, so the pitches word wraps around the letter for new

blocks.note: patter is a salesman's glib talk
N abbreviates new

explanation.surface: A salesman spins his lines about the latest models.
explanation.definitionFit: Patterns are models or templates to be copied.

clue.text: Big game repeatedly spotted in vast estates there

indicators.note: spotted in means seen inside, so the letters sit within the following words; repeatedly is surface colour for wildlife sightings

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A safari: large wild animals are often seen roaming huge estates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big game' suggests safari animals, but it is a Test match, a five-day international cricket fixture; 'repeatedly' nods to how often Tests are played.
explanation.definitionFit: A Test is a major international cricket match, the biggest game in the sport.

clue.text: Play in attempt to win a hand?

definitions.text: Play in attempt to win a hand?

blocks.clueFragment: Play in attempt to win a hand?
blocks.note: surface reading: a move in a card game aimed at taking a trick

blocks.clueFragment: Play in attempt to win a hand?
blocks.note: setter's reading: music performed to win a lover's hand in marriage

explanation.surface: A card player makes a bid to take the trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hand' suggests cards; here it is a hand in marriage, and 'play' is music.
explanation.definitionFit: A serenade is a song played or sung beneath a beloved's window to woo them.

clue.text: Doctor wearing protective gear for fighting

indicators.note: someone wearing clothes is inside them, so the doctor goes within the garment

blocks.note: a coat protects against weather
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A medic dons armour to go into battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Combat is fighting, especially between armed forces.

clue.text: One or two girls providing shrub

blocks.note: Rose is a girl's name
Mary is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl or two have brought along a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One or two girls' works both ways: Rosemary is one girl's name, or Rose and Mary are two.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosemary is an aromatic evergreen shrub used as a herb.

clue.text: Insult that's small, easy to bear

blocks.note: first meaning: a snub or affront
second meaning: minor, not serious

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one small insult that is easy to shrug off; the word works as a noun and an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A slight is a snub; slight as an adjective means minor, trivial and so easy to put up with.

clue.text: Stupid person the day before helping to produce solemn statement

blocks.note: an ass is a fool
an eve is the day before an event
a ration is a portion, a helping

explanation.surface: A fool, on the eve of something, helps draft a grave declaration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Helping' looks like a verb, but it is a noun: a portion of food.
explanation.definitionFit: An asseveration is an earnest, solemn declaration or assertion.

clue.text: Going either way in metropolis, I located food store

indicators.note: in means contained within, and going either way says the letters read correctly forwards or backwards inside the words

blocks.note: letters spanning the end of the city word, the I and the start of located

explanation.surface: Someone tracking down a grocery store in the big city, from either direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going either way' tells you it works both forwards and backwards: it also sits reversed inside metropOLIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A silo is a tower or pit for storing grain or fodder, a food store.

clue.text: Enthusiastic support, having very briefly contributed

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so only an abbreviation of the word is kept
having something contributed means taking it inside, so the short form goes into the support word

blocks.note: aid is support
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: Keen backing, since someone chipped in for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: An avid fan is eager and enthusiastic.

clue.text: Autocrat, identified as terrible, reformed in vain

indicators.note: reformed means made over in a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dreadful tyrant tried to reform himself, but to no avail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible' looks like criticism, but it is part of the ruler's title: Ivan the Terrible.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan IV of Russia, the first tsar, is known to history as Ivan the Terrible.

clue.text: That chap and I, holding pound, invest capital in Europe

indicators.note: holding means gripping inside, so the outer words close round what follows

blocks.note: he is that chap
L for libra, the pound
to sink money into something is to invest it
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two people pool their money to put capital into Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' and 'invest' suggest finance, but the capital is a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Helsinki is the capital city of Finland.

clue.text: Apart from revolutionary in old hat, turned back

indicators.note: turned back means facing the other way, so the word is read backwards
in means placed inside, so the revolutionary goes within the other word

blocks.note: old hat means out of date
Che Guevara, the Argentine revolutionary

explanation.surface: Apart from a rebel in an old hat who turned round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old hat' looks like headgear for the revolutionary but means outdated.
explanation.definitionFit: Detached means separated or standing apart from others.
